Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "need a handoff document for the team document migration, and send it to Nadia, not Otis. it should be something the people doing the move can use, not a message saying the move is finished. We are planning to move material from the Operations Shared drive into the Beacon workspace. The team has fourteen people across Research, Support, and Administration. Research has 214 documents, Support has 173, and Administration has 99, so 486 altogether. Keep those counts in the handoff and say which group each count belongs to. The counts are from the inventory that Mina circulated on 6 May; don't present them as a fresh count made during migration. The inventory includes working files and reference documents, but it doesn't include personal folders.

The proposed work window is Tuesday 12 May through Thursday 14 May 2026. Tuesday is for Research, Wednesday for Support, and Thursday for Administration. That's the proposed sequence, not a confirmation that anyone has started or finished. The team has a check-in at 10:30 each morning, and the handoff should mention it as a place to raise access problems or a file that looks missing. Don't make up a check-in location or an organizer. The people doing the move should compare the source and destination folder totals after each group's transfer, but there isn't a specific reconciliation tool named yet. Say that plainly instead of picking one.

The destination has three top-level folders named Research, Support, and Administration. Inside each one, keep the existing project-folder names and put reference documents in a folder called Reference only where that folder already exists in the source. Some source folders have no Reference folder, and nobody has asked for a new one. We don't want a redesigned taxonomy as part of this request. Keep the project folder names as they are, including punctuation, even when two names seem similar. We know there are projects called “Harbor renewal” and “Harbor-renewal”; don't merge them. The handoff should explain this because a person doing a quick tidy might think those are duplicates.

For permissions, the 11 documents marked restricted in Mina's inventory need their current access checked before they are moved. The inventory doesn't say which individual people should have access, so don't put names against those documents. If the current access cannot be confirmed, leave that document in the source for now and list its filename and source folder in an exceptions table. This is a condition, not a request to copy it first and sort permissions out later. Seven of the restricted documents are in Research, three in Support, and one in Administration. We also have nine signed vendor agreements in Administration that should remain in the source; list those separately from permission exceptions, and don't imply that anyone has decided when they will move. The rest of the Administration files are still part of the planned transfer.

There are 38 documents that were updated in the last 90 days. The inventory marks them with a blue dot, but the blue dot is not a priority label and shouldn't be treated as a reason to move them first. Keep their current folder locations during the transfer. We don't have a separate list of those 38 filenames in the notes I have, so don't manufacture one. It would be useful for the handoff to tell the team to use Mina's inventory to identify them. The main goal is to keep the current organization recognizable and make it possible to check what moved, not to decide which documents matter most.

Please include a numbered sequence of the work, with the inventory and folder check before transfer, the permission check for those 11 restricted documents, the group-by-group transfer during the proposed dates, and a comparison of source and destination folder totals after each group. Keep the conditional handling of restricted files in the right place in that sequence. The handoff can say that a file without confirmed access stays in the source and goes on the exceptions table. It should not claim that all 486 documents will necessarily move, since the nine agreements are staying behind and restricted documents may also be left behind. Ask the team to record the final transferred counts by group, but don't supply counts that we don't know yet.

Include this exact quote from Jo in Research: “Please keep the folder names familiar; we lose time when a project gets renamed halfway through a handoff.” It is a comment about retaining the names, not authorization to change any folder. The handoff should make clear that the quote does not override the instruction to keep the source names unchanged. There are no migration results yet, no completed access review, and no approval from a manager mentioned in the notes. Keep the document in planning terms and don't imply otherwise.

One more thing for the last part: Records asked that the handoff include a separate note that existing links to files may need checking after transfer. They have not supplied a link list, and they didn't ask us to repair links as part of this migration. Include that request without turning it into a promise that every link will work or be fixed. ### Inventory and folder structure

Mina circulated the inventory on 6 May. It lists working files and reference documents, but not personal folders. Keep “Harbor renewal” and “Harbor-renewal” as separate project folders; do not merge them. Put reference documents in a folder named Reference only if that folder already exists in the corresponding source folder. Do not create new Reference folders. Jo in Research said, “Please keep the folder names familiar; we lose time when a project gets renamed halfway through a handoff.” Treat this as a comment about retaining familiar names, not permission to rename anything; keep source folder names unchanged.

### Planned work window and sequence

The proposed work window is Tuesday 12 May through Thursday 14 May 2026, in this order: Research on Tuesday, Support on Wednesday, and Administration on Thursday. This is a proposed sequence, not confirmation that work has begun or finished. The team has a 10:30 check-in each morning for raising access problems or files that appear to be missing. Do not specify a location or organizer, as neither is provided.

Use this numbered sequence for the work:
1. Review Mina’s inventory and check the source folders before transfer. Use the inventory to identify the 38 documents updated in the last 90 days; they are marked with a blue dot. The dot is not a priority label, and these documents should remain in their current folder locations. The notes do not provide a separate filename list for them, so do not create one.
2. Before moving the 11 documents marked restricted in the inventory, check whether their current access can be confirmed. The inventory does not identify which individual people should have access, so do not assign names. If access cannot be confirmed, leave the document in the source and list its filename and source folder in an exceptions table. Do not move it first and resolve permissions afterward. 3. Transfer the groups in the proposed order and during the proposed dates above. Keep the existing folder organization and names.
4. After each group’s transfer, compare the source and destination folder totals. No reconciliation tool has been named; do not select one on the team’s behalf. Ask the team to record final transferred counts by group, without supplying counts that are not yet known.

### Items to remain in the source

Nine signed vendor agreements in Administration should remain in the source and be listed separately from permission exceptions. The notes do not say when they might move. The rest of the Administration files remain part of the planned transfer. Do not state that all 486 inventory documents will necessarily move: the agreements are staying behind, and restricted documents may also remain in the source if their access cannot be confirmed.

The handoff should focus on keeping the current organization recognizable and making it possible to check what moved, not on deciding which documents matter most. Do not present the blue-dot documents as priority items.

Records asked for a separate note that existing file links may need checking after transfer. They have not supplied a link list and did not ask the team to repair links as part of this migration.
